why_relevant: Regional trade-portal page describing Kosovo's procurement regime and access points in English; useful for regime comparison across the Western Balkans and for confirming the official entry points from a neutral multilateral source.

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering Kosovo (TendersInfo, BidDetail, GlobalTenders, TendersOnTime)
why_relevant: Paywalled English-language resellers of Kosovo notices. Their free teaser listings are occasionally useful for keyword discovery (e.g. surfacing that an ATM or core-banking lot exists), but they are intermediaries with unknown latency and coverage — never a substitute for the platform.

Publishes underlying procurement documents alongside reporting (observed: a piece with source documents on the KEK procurement chief annulling a tender). Documents that authorities remove from their own sites sometimes survive only in this kind of reporting — a useful archival/reveals-indirectly source for the POE segment.

source_name: EU u Srbiji / euzatebe.rs — 'EU javni pozivi' (EU calls listing, sr)
why_relevant: EU Delegation-run Serbian-language listing of EU calls and tenders; a model for how EU-channel notices are localised in sr, and occasionally carries regional/multi-country calls that include Kosovo. Useful for sr-language terminology harvesting ('javni pozivi', 'EU tenderi').

Commercial aggregator that states it harvests Kosovo's official authority and agency websites and organises notices into searchable categories. Its category tree is a useful hint at which Kosovo buyers publish outside the central portal.

High-velocity Albanian-language news portal in Kosovo built around speed and originality of breaking items. Low editorial filter means bank/vendor press releases and contract-signing photo-ops appear here early; value is timing, not analysis.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — official Facebook page
why_relevant: In Kosovo, Facebook is often the fastest-updated channel for event announcements and photo/agenda posts naming speakers and sponsoring vendors.

source_name: Kosovo.energy — republisher of MCC/MFK Specific Procurement Notices in Albanian
why_relevant: Sector news site that reproduces MFK 'Njoftim Specifik për Prokurim (NSP)' notices in Albanian alongside the English SPN. Useful as a bilingual terminology anchor and as a mirror when MFK rotates notices off its site.

Prishtina/Skopje custom software firm active in the Kosovo banking-tech ecosystem (co-organiser with ProCredit Bank Kosova of DevCon Prishtina). Sponsorship/partnership visibility is a weak but real signal of commercial relationships with banks; its portfolio pages may name bank clients.

Publishes document-led stories alleging unlawful tender awards by state-owned enterprises, naming officials and beneficiary firms; low institutional credibility but occasionally first to publish underlying contract documents.

source_name: Posta e Kosovës / NPOSTA — postal payment and counter services terms
why_relevant: The postal operator runs a nationwide counter network used for bill payment and cash services — a publicly-owned, procurement-law-bound buyer of counter terminals, cash handling and payment integration, and a possible agent for remittance firms.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International - Code of Conduct for Suppliers / group procurement governance
why_relevant: RBI Group Procurement (headed at group level) sets binding rules that Raiffeisen Kosovo applies, including anti-collusion clauses that forbid suppliers disclosing anything about planned, running or pending RBI Group procurements. That clause itself is intelligence: it explains why Raiffeisen Kosovo notices are thin publicly and why vendor-side sources will be silent. The RBI platform login page is the entry point to group vendor-facing platforms.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës — The Kosovo Banker (issuu archive)
why_relevant: Industry magazine where acquirers, processors and fintechs describe deployments (contactless, tapXphone/softPOS, open APIs) and where vendors advertise — an efficient, dated record of who supplies whom in Kosovo payments, including non-bank players partnering with banks.
